title: Design History and Architecture
text: ibger grew applied data work Secretaria de Projetos Estratégicos (Strategic Projects Office) Pernambuco state government, collaboration Universidade Federal de Pernambuco (UFPE). teams routinely build indicators Brazilian official statistics — census tables, price indices, agricultural labor surveys — IBGE disseminates aggregate tables SIDRA exposes programmatically via IBGE Aggregates API v3. existing R client, sidrar, targets legacy SIDRA API: different endpoint family positional string parameters, programmatic access v3 metadata endpoints, hard value cap leaves user work around. Repeated -house scripting v3 API — building URLs hand, decoding nested JSON, rediscovering undocumented failure modes — motivated proper package. Development proceeded three stages: Initial version (early 2026, ibger 0.1.0 CRAN). first public version already contained core current design: discovery functions (ibge_aggregates(), ibge_metadata(), ibge_periods(), ibge_localities()), main data-retrieval function (ibge_variables()) returning tidy long-format tibbles, pre-flight validation query parameters cached metadata, session-level metadata cache, parse_ibge_value() helper IBGE’s special value codes, SIDRA URL translator (parse_sidra_url() / fetch_sidra_url()) migrating existing SIDRA/sidrar workflows. version developed -house — ideas iterated internal analysis scripts package existed — pushed GitHub essentially complete prepared CRAN submission. public git history begins single large “cran ready” commit rather long series incremental ones: incremental history happened scripts local iterations predate repository. Shortly initial release added Metadata API v2 client (survey catalog methodological metadata), Shiny catalog explorer, README comparison sidrar prompted early user questions. Automatic chunking (July 2026, ibger 0.2.0). first external feature request (repo issue #1, @danielvartan) asked retrieve tables whose result size exceeds API’s per-request value limit. splitting queries hand internally; version 0.2.0 moved logic package. ibge_variables() now estimates result size query sending , estimate exceeds limit, transparently splits query — periods first, localities — binds pieces single tibble. Determining real limit required empirical testing: API documents 100,000 values per request, requests reliably fail HTTP 500 well (44,560-value request succeeds; 50,130 fails), default limit 50,000 observations recorded R/chunking.R. rOpenSci preparation (July 2026). preparation review test suite expanded chunking-unit tests ~87% coverage exported functions, using httptest2 recorded fixtures suite runs offline; CI (R CMD check three platforms, coverage upload Codecov) community files (CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, codemeta.json) added; JOSS paper drafted. None changed public API. disclosed submission, recent development (tests, documentation, paper drafting) assisted LLM coding tool (Claude Code), generated content reviewed, executed validated authors. architecture API design described human decisions predate assistance.

title: Understanding the IBGE Aggregate Data API
text: API rejects requests whose result large, answering HTTP 500. documented limit 100,000 values per request, computed : variables × categories × periods × localities ≤ 100,000 practice requests start failing roughly 50,000 values, limit ibger uses. example, request aggregate 2654 (deaths month, nature, sex age) : Classification 244: 1 category Classification 1836: 2 categories Classification 2: 2 categories Classification 260: 1 category 6 periods (default) 4 municipalities produces 1 × 2 × 2 × 1 × 6 × 4 = 96 values — well within limit. need split large requests . ibge_variables() estimates size result metadata (fetching period locality lists needed) , estimate exceeds limit, splits query — first periods, localities — binds pieces back together. chunk argument controls : TRUE (default) uses built-limit, FALSE forces single request, number sets custom per-request limit. title: ibger: Access the IBGE Aggregate Data API from R
text: sidrar closest alternative. packages access IBGE aggregate data, talk different APIs hosted IBGE: Different endpoints: sidrar uses legacy SIDRA API (apisidra.ibge.gov.br/values), ibger uses IBGE Aggregates API v3 (servicodados.ibge.gov.br/api/v3/agregados). IBGE’s documentation describes Aggregates API standardized version SIDRA API. practical size limit: SIDRA API caps responses 20,000 rows (sidrar’s error message: “20k values”) leaves splitting user. ibger estimates result size querying , exceeds Aggregates API per-request limit, automatically splits query multiple requests combines results (ibge_variables(..., chunk = TRUE), default). Note large requests slow server side: municipality-level queries (localities = "N6") can take one several minutes per request answered IBGE API — function hanging. Structured metadata: ibger queries dedicated JSON endpoints metadata (/metadados, /periodos, /localidades/{nivel}). sidrar scrapes HTML page (desctabapi.aspx) discover classifications, info_sidra() opens metadata web browser rather returning data. Parameter ergonomics: sidrar requires positional string codes (classific = "c315", geo = "City", geo.filter = list("State" = 50)), ibger uses standard R objects (classification = list("315" = 7169), localities = list(N6 = 5002704)). Pre-flight validation: ibger checks parameters (levels, periods, variables, classifications) aggregate metadata hitting API. Invalid requests fail fast clear error messages showing allowed values, instead returning opaque API error. Modern stack: ibger uses httr2 (automatic retry, structured error handling), cli (progress messages), returns tibbles default. sidrar uses httr v1 retry mechanism.

text: Brazilian Institute Geography Statistics (IBGE) agency responsible Brazil’s official statistics, conducting national demographic census dozens recurring demographic, economic, social agricultural surveys. results disseminated aggregate tables SIDRA (Sistema IBGE de Recuperação Automática) exposed programmatically IBGE Aggregates API [@ibgeapi] — time writing, 9,278 tables 70 surveys. ibger R [@rcore] package provides complete, tidyverse-friendly [@tidyverse] interface API. Users can discover tables (ibge_aggregates()), inspect variables, classifications categories (ibge_metadata()), list available periods localities, retrieve data (ibge_variables()) combination variables, periods, geographic levels — whole country 5,570 municipalities — classification categories. Every function returns tidy tibble long format, ready analysis standard tidyverse workflows. package also covers IBGE Metadata API (survey catalog methodological documentation) ships interactive Shiny explorer browsing table catalog. title: Summary
text: IBGE data underpin quantitative research Brazil. Demographic Census, conducted since 1872 recently 2022, country’s fundamental source population counts sampling frame household surveys; IPCA consumer price index official inflation measure targeted Central Bank Brazil; municipal GDP, PNAD Contínua labor-force survey municipal agricultural surveys (PAM, PPM) anchor studies economics, demography, public health, agriculture regional planning. SIDRA canonical channel aggregates reach public, reproducible research requires scripted, validated access rather manual downloads website. main existing R client, sidrar [@sidrar], accesses legacy SIDRA API served community well, inherits API’s constraints: 20,000-value limit per request built-work-around, metadata discovery via HTML scraping, pre-flight validation, positional string-coded parameters. ibger targets modern Aggregates API v3, whose structured JSON metadata endpoints make fundamentally different design possible (validation, size estimation automatic chunking, described ). ibger also complements growing ecosystem R packages Brazilian public data: geobr [@geobr] distributes IBGE’s official spatial data sets, censobr [@censobr] provides census microdata, PNADcIBGE [@pnadcibge] covers labor-survey microdata. None accesses aggregate tables SIDRA, precisely layer ibger covers; example shows, packages compose naturally. ibger grew production needs Pernambuco’s Strategic Monitoring Data Science Team, builds R-based data solutions monitoring state public policies [@medeiros2025], aimed researchers, statistical agencies, journalists analysts need reliable, reproducible pipelines Brazilian official statistics.

title: Summary
text: Three design decisions distinguish ibger. First, queries validated request sent: parameters checked cached table metadata, invalid variables, periods, localities categories produce immediate, informative errors listing allowed values. Second, results transparently chunked: Aggregates API rejects large requests (empirically, roughly 50,000 values, although documented limit 100,000), ibger estimates result size advance — variables × periods × localities × categories — automatically splits oversized queries multiple requests, periods localities, combining single tibble. full extraction table 1612 (municipal crop production: 8 variables × 6 years × 5,570 municipalities, 267,000 values) therefore works box instead failing HTTP error. Third, parse_sidra_url() fetch_sidra_url() translate legacy SIDRA API URLs (SIDRA Query Builder existing sidrar scripts) equivalent ibger calls, easing migration cross-checking. HTTP handling built httr2 [@httr2] automatic retries; metadata, period locality lookups cached per session; IBGE’s special value codes (zero, suppressed, available) converted parse_ibge_value(). package tested recorded API fixtures, behaviour verified offline.

title: Get variable data from an aggregate — ibge_variables
text: aggregate Numeric aggregate identifier (SIDRA table). variable Variable(s) retrieve. Can : NULL (default): returns standard variables Numeric vector: specific IDs, e.g. c(284, 285) "": includes automatically generated percentage variables periods Period(s) query. Can : Negative integer: last N periods, e.g. -6 (default) Numeric vector: e.g. c(201701, 201702, 201703) String range: e.g. "201701-201712" localities Locality(ies) query. Can : "BR" (default): Brazil Level code: "N3" (states), "N6" (municipalities) Named list specific localities: list(N3 = c(33, 35)) (RJ SP states), list(N6 = c(3550308, 3304557)) (SP RJ municipalities) classification Classification(s) filter results. Named list names classification IDs values category ID vectors. Use "" categories. E.g. list("226" = c(4844, 96608), "218" = 4780) view Display mode: NULL (default), "OLAP" "flat". validate Logical. TRUE (default), validates parameters aggregate metadata querying. Use FALSE skip. chunk Controls automatic splitting large queries. IBGE API rejects requests whose result large HTTP 500 error (documented limit 100,000 values, practice requests fail 50,000). Can : TRUE (default): estimates result size (variables x periods x localities x categories) , exceeds 50,000 values, transparently splits query multiple smaller requests (periods, localities) combines results. FALSE: always performs single request. Positive number: TRUE, custom per-request value limit.
